facts.claim: Anthropic: structured outputs guarantee schema-compliant responses through constrained decoding; your JSON schema is compiled into a grammar that constrains Claude's output.

Anthropic: objects must set additionalProperties to false; recursive schemas, numerical constraints (minimum, maximum) and string constraints (minLength, maxLength) are not supported, and an unsupported feature returns a 400 error.
Anthropic: the first time you use a schema there is extra latency while the grammar compiles; compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours from last use.

Anthropic: when Claude refuses, the response has stop_reason "refusal", you are billed for the tokens generated, and the output may not match your schema, because the refusal takes precedence over the schema.
Anthropic: when the answer hits max_tokens, the output may be incomplete and not match your schema; retry with a higher max_tokens.
OpenAI: JSON mode gives valid JSON, but only Structured Outputs ensure the answer follows your schema.
OpenAI: every field must be required and additionalProperties must be false; a schema may have up to 5,000 object properties, 10 levels of nesting and 1,000 enum values.
OpenAI: a refusal comes back in its own refusal field and may not follow your schema, so check for it before parsing.
OpenAI: an answer can be cut off when it reaches the max tokens limit; the response is then marked incomplete and should not be parsed as finished.

XGrammar (Dong and colleagues, 2024) runs context-free grammars for constrained decoding; it splits the vocabulary into tokens that can be checked ahead of time and tokens checked at run time, for up to 100× speedup over earlier engines.
llguidance computes the token mask in about 50 microseconds of CPU time per token for a 128k-token vocabulary; it powers OpenAI's Structured Outputs and is integrated in vLLM and llama.cpp.

Guidance's token healing backs up one token before the end of the prompt and makes the first generated token start with that token's text, so the model can use the split it learned in training. A trailing space in a prompt is almost always a bad idea in GPT models.
